triage.notes: 地方紙による単発症例報告で、マラリアは同地域の風土病であり通常の医療対応が行われている。

article.articleHeadline: Gastroenterite causou a morte de cinco garimpeiros de ouro na província do Bengo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Gastroenteritis killed five gold prospectors in Bengo Province.
article.articleSummary: Five gold prospectors in Bula Atumba, Bengo Province, Angola, died from gastroenteritis linked to contaminated water. Provincial health director Matondo Alexandre announced laboratory results from samples taken earlier this month, tying infections to the Machadão locality at the Bananeira mining site beside the Lumbinge River. Of 32 patients treated at the Bula Atumba General Hospital, five deaths were recorded (two in-hospital, three community), with 27 patients discharged. The cases occur in the same area where a May landslide at an illegal gold mine killed 28 people. Initial theories of chemical water poisoning and cholera were ruled out by tests conducted at reference laboratories in Luanda and Bengo. The confirmed cause is gastroenteritis due to multiple bacteria in the water, causing diarrhea, vomiting, nausea, and abdominal pain; all patients were from the mining zone.

triage.headline_ja: アンゴラ・ベンゴ州で金採掘者5人が胃腸炎で死亡
triage.triage_reason: 感染源は特定の汚染水域に限定された細菌性胃腸炎であり、コレラは検査で否定された。発生国アンゴラは対象国リストに含まれず、国際的拡大の懸念も低い。
triage.notes: 当初コレラが疑われたが、ルアンダおよびベンゴの検査機関により否定され、水中の複数菌による胃腸炎と確定された。感染は違法金鉱山（Bananeira鉱区）作業員に限定されており、ヒト-ヒト感染や地域拡大の証拠はない。発生国アンゴラは対象国リストに該当しないため、verified_locationsは空とした。

article.articleHeadline: Walking in flood water? Here's how Mumbai doctors say you can protect yourself from leptospirosis
article.articleSummary: As of 9 July 2026, heavy Monsoon rainfall in Mumbai and the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR) — including Thane, Vasai-Virar, and Nalasopara — has caused flooding and waterlogging, forcing residents to walk through submerged streets. The article highlights leptospirosis risk linked to floodwater exposure and cites guidance from Mumbai doctors on protective measures, though specific recommendations are not detailed. There are no case counts, deaths, laboratory confirmations, or outbreak status provided. The piece underscores the ongoing mobility disruptions due to flooding and the potential for leptospirosis transmission in submerged urban environments during the monsoon season in the MMR.

triage.headline_ja: 洪水の中を歩いていますか？ムンバイの医師が語るレプトスピラ症からの身の守り方
triage.triage_reason: モンスーンによる洪水でレプトスピラ症のリスクが指摘されているが、症例数・死亡者数・発生確認等の具体的情報がなく、季節性の注意喚起記事にとどまるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 毎年のモンスーン季に見られる注意喚起記事であり、具体的な症例数や公衆衛生への影響の記載はない。続報で実際の感染者数増加等があればPICKUPへの格上げを検討。

article.articleHeadline: Nord-Kivu : l'OMS analyse les défis liés à la riposte contre Ebola à Beni - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: North Kivu: WHO analyzes the challenges related to the Ebola response in Beni - ACP
article.articleSummary: North Kivu, Democratic Republic of Congo — On 9 July 2026, a World Health Organization delegation visiting Beni analyzes challenges in the Ebola virus disease response. Led by Dr. Chikwe Ihekweazu, the mission aims to map ongoing containment efforts, identify obstacles, and strengthen collaboration with partners and the Congolese state to allow the population to resume normal activities. The visit included discussions with North Kivu Governor Evariste Somo Kakule on the area’s epidemiological situation. Ihekweazu urged residents to trust the Ebola care system and seek care promptly when fever or related symptoms appear, noting that authorities and partners are exerting maximum effort to address health challenges. He called for broad community engagement to achieve Ebola eradication.

triage.headline_ja: 北キブ州：WHOがベニでのエボラ対応の課題を分析
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国北キブ州でエボラウイルス病の対応が継続中であり、WHOが現地訪問して課題分析を行うなど、重症度・人道支援ニーズの高い進行中の公衆衛生危機であるため。
triage.notes: 記事はエボラ流行の新規発生ではなく、既存のアウトブレイクに対するWHOの現地対応状況・課題分析を報じたもの。ベニ地域での対応継続とコミュニティエンゲージメントの必要性が強調されている。

article.articleHeadline: मुंह से लार, पैरों में घाव... गांवों में चुपके से पैर पसार रही यह पशु बीमारी
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Drooling from the mouth, sores on the feet... this livestock disease is quietly spreading through villages.
article.articleSummary: Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD) is spreading in Shahjahanpur, Uttar Pradesh, India, during the monsoon season. This highly contagious viral illness affects cloven-hoofed animals—cattle, buffalo, sheep, and goats—causing high fever, mouth and hoof ulcers, drooling, and lameness, which can impair feeding and reduce milk production. Without timely action, outbreaks cause significant economic losses to farmers. Prevention hinges on vaccination under India’s National Animal Disease Control Programme, typically administered twice yearly, with a recommendation to vaccinate before the monsoon. Farm management emphasizes hygiene: keep stables dry and clean, apply lime or phenyl, disinfectant for floors, and use separate feeding and watering bowls for sick animals; wash wounds with potassium permanganate. If illness is suspected, isolate affected animals and consult a veterinarian rather than relying on home remedies, and quarantine new stock during outbreaks.

triage.headline_ja: 口からよだれ、足に潰瘍…この家畜の病気が村々でひそかに広がっている
triage.triage_reason: 動物のみが罹患する口蹄疫の地域的発生であり、ヒトへの公衆衛生影響はなく、国際的拡大や渡航・貿易制限のリスクも示されていない。
triage.notes: 家畜（牛・水牛・羊・ヤギ）の口蹄疫に関する地方ニュースで、ヒトへの感染や公衆衛生上の緊急性は言及されていない。ワクチン接種と衛生管理の推奨が主内容。

article.articleHeadline: Ebolautbrottet det snabbast växande i historien
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak, the fastest-growing in history.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-07-09, the Ebola outbreak is described as the fastest-growing in history, with 500 deaths and 1,759 confirmed infections reported over the past three days. In eastern China, 28 people died in a fire at a shoe factory in Chendai, Fujian Province. CCTV reported 35 fire engines and 183 firefighters were deployed, with videos circulating showing people on the building's roof pleading for help. President Xi Jinping has called for a rapid investigation into the fire's cause and for those responsible to be held to account, according to Xinhua. No information on hospitalizations or imported cases is provided in this article.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ流行、史上最速の拡大
triage.triage_reason: 史上最速の拡大とされるエボラ流行で3日間に500人死亡・1759人感染という深刻な公衆衛生影響が報告されており、IHR基準に複数該当するためフルRRAでの確認が必要。ただし発生国は記事中で明示されていない。
triage.notes: 記事はエボラ流行の統計（3日間で500人死亡、1759人感染）と中国福建省の靴工場火災という無関係な2つの事件を並記したものであり、Bluedotが付与した中国の地域情報は火災事故の発生地であり、エボラ流行の発生国とは無関係。エボラ流行の発生国名は記事中に記載がなく特定不能。対象国との関連は現時点で確認できないため、続報でエボラ流行の発生国情報を確認する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Malaria, dengue cases down as GVMC steps up in preventive measures in Visakhapatnam
article.articleSummary: Visakhapatnam’s GVMC reports declines in malaria and dengue in 2026 versus 2025 after intensified vector control. Malaria: 91 cases in 2025, 74 in Jan–Jul; this year about 30 in the same period. Dengue: 323 cases in 2025, 138 in Jan–Jul 2025; around 81 so far in 2026. Gajuwaka is the most malaria-affected zone; for dengue, North, South and East zones report the highest counts. Open drains are cited as a major driver; Chikungunya had 13 cases in 2025; none so far this year. Containment includes surveillance and anti-vector measures within about 100 surrounding households per positive case; anti-larval operations, source reduction, insecticide spraying. Drones sprayed anti-larval insecticides in 206 water bodies; regular knapsack spraying and fogging continue. GVMC plans about 100 additional seasonal workers and will release Gambusia fish (target ~20 lakh this year). Coordination with KGH; residents urged to eliminate water stagnation.

triage.headline_ja: ヴィシャカパトナムでGVMCの予防対策強化によりマラリア・デング症例が減少
triage.triage_reason: マラリア・デング・チクングニアいずれも前年比で症例数が減少しており、地方自治体による通常の対策が効果を上げているという内容で、公衆衛生上の異常事態や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 症例数は前年より減少傾向であり、地元自治体（GVMC）による通常の媒介動物対策の成果を報告する内容。シグナルとしての緊急性は低い。

article.articleHeadline: Congo: nouveaux cas d'Ebola suspectés dans une province épargnée
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Congo: New Suspected Ebola Cases in a Province That Has Been Spared
article.articleSummary: Two new suspected Ebola cases were reported in Kisangani, Tshopo, central-northern DR Congo, as the outbreak extends to regions previously spared. Nationally, confirmed cases rise to 1,759 with 600 deaths in the latest outbreak. One suspected case is tied to the Nia-Nia health zone in Ituri; the other has no apparent geographic link to known clusters. Transmission continues, aided by population movement and insecurity, with several treatment centers nearing capacity (per WHO representative Anne Ancia). Health workers in Ituri report nonpayment since the outbreak began, limited protective equipment, and harsh treatment by authorities and local communities. Bunia airport closure hinders the response and funding flows. The resurgence is driven by the Bundibugyo Ebola virus, for which no vaccine or approved treatment exists; researchers began a highly anticipated clinical trial last week. The outbreak was declared on May 15 by Congolese authorities according to the WHO.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ:これまで感染がなかった州で新たなエボラ疑い症例
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱の感染拡大が継続しており、これまで感染のなかった州(キサンガニ)にも波及。死者600人、確定症例1,759人に達し、ワクチン・治療薬が存在しないブンディブギョ株による流行でIHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: ブンディブギョ型エボラウイルスによる流行で、ワクチン・承認済み治療法が存在しない。医療従事者への未払い、防護具不足、ブニア空港閉鎖による資金・対応の遅延など、対応能力に深刻な課題があり、国際支援が急務。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola death toll in Congo tops 600. New cases also suspected in previously unaffected provinces
article.articleSummary: On 2026-07-09, Congo's Ebola outbreak has 600 deaths among 1,759 confirmed cases. New suspected infections appear in Kisangani (Kisangani in Tshopo) and Haut-Uele, indicating spread beyond the Ituri epicenter. Two suspected cases in Kisangani; one linked to Nia-Nia in Ituri, the other with no clear geographic link. The government declared the fresh outbreak on May 15 after weeks of undetected transmission. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo virus, a rare strain with no approved vaccine or treatment. Last week, treatment trials began in a bid to counter the virus. Containment is hampered by funding gaps, attacks on health centers, and ongoing eastern Congo conflict, authorities say, with monitoring supported by the World Health Organization.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ死者数が600人を超える。これまで感染がなかった州でも新たな症例が疑われる
triage.triage_reason: DRCで確認症例1,759例、死者600人に達する大規模エボラ流行が発生し、震源地イトゥリ州を超えてキサンガニやオートウエレ州にも拡大の兆候があり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: 希少株であるブンディブギョウイルスによる流行で、承認されたワクチン・治療法が存在しない点、資金不足・医療施設への攻撃・東部コンゴ紛争が対応を阻害している点が特に懸念される。WHOによるモニタリング支援が行われている。

article.articleHeadline: L'épidémie actuelle d'Ebola se propage plus rapidement que toutes les précédentes
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The current Ebola outbreak is spreading faster than any previous outbreaks.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-07-09, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is spreading faster than any prior outbreak, with 1,759 laboratory-confirmed cases and 600 deaths since its May start. Africa CDC emergency lead Dr. Wessam Mankoula warned that the virus is outpacing the response, spreading more quickly than the resources deployed, and that this pace applies to all Ebola virus variants, not only Bundibugyo. The Bundibugyo virus, to date, has no vaccine or specific treatment. The World Health Organization’s situation report notes the broader outbreak in the DRC, while neighboring Uganda reports 20 confirmed cases and 2 deaths. The DRC has endured 17 Ebola outbreaks; ongoing transmission emphasizes critical gaps in control measures and underscores the urgent need for effective countermeasures and strengthened health-system responses.

triage.headline_ja: 現在のエボラ流行は過去のどの流行よりも速いスピードで拡大している
triage.triage_reason: DRCで過去最速のエボラ流行が発生し、隣国ウガンダにも拡大、致死率・症例数ともに重大でIHR基準を複数満たすためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: ウガンダも症例報告があるが対象国リストに含まれないため、verified_locationsはDRCのみとした。Bundibugyoウイルスにはワクチン・特異的治療法がない点は重要なリスク要因。

article.articleHeadline: Congo suspects new Ebola cases in previously unaffected province
article.articleSummary: Two new suspected Ebola cases in Kisangani, Tshopo province, Congo, with one linked to Nia-Nia health zone in Ituri and the other with no apparent link to known outbreaks. The death toll in the latest Congo Ebola outbreak reaches 600, while total confirmed cases nationwide rise to 1,759. The outbreak began in Ituri and has spread to other regions; Kisangani is in north-central Congo near Ituri, where cases had not previously been recorded. The virus is Bundibugyo, a rare strain with no approved vaccine or treatment; a clinical trial was launched last week. Transmission is fueled by population movements and insecurity; treatment centers are near capacity. Bunia airport is closed, complicating response and funds flow; health workers have gone unpaid since the outbreak declaration on 15 May. WHO official Anne Ancia notes ongoing strain; authorities report concerns are being addressed, but attacks and scepticism persist.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ、これまで感染が確認されていなかった州で新たなエボラ疑い症例
triage.triage_reason: コンゴのエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクは死者600人・確定症例1759人に達し、新たな未感染州（チョポ州キサンガニ）への拡大が疑われている。稀な株（ブンディブギョ）で承認ワクチン・治療法がなく、治安悪化や資金不足も重なり深刻な公衆衛生上の脅威。
triage.notes: 新規症例はキサンガニ（チョポ州）で確認され、これまでの流行地イツリ州から拡大している可能性。ブンイア空港閉鎖や医療従事者への未払い、治安悪化が対応を複雑化させている。

article.articleHeadline: В Конго подозревают новые случаи Эболы в ранее чистой провинции
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In Congo, new Ebola cases suspected in a previously Ebola-free province.
article.articleSummary: New suspected Ebola cases emerge in Kisangani, Chopo Province, in north-central Democratic Republic of Congo, near Ituri where the outbreak began. Government says two new suspects; one linked to Ni-Nia health zone in Ituri, the other with no obvious link to known foci. The country’s latest Ebola outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which there is currently no approved vaccine or treatment. Last outbreak in DRC produced about 600 deaths, with total confirmed cases rising to 1,759. The virus continues to spread amid population movement and unstable security conditions; treatment centers are near capacity. Healthcare workers in Ituri report unpaid salaries since the outbreak’s declaration, prompting protests, while Bunia airport shutdown hampers response and funds flow. WHO notes outbreak declared May 15; researchers began a long-awaited clinical trial for a therapy against Bundibugyo ebolavirus.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴで、これまでエボラ感染がなかった州で新たな疑い症例
triage.triage_reason: DRCのエボラ流行が新たな未感染州（キサンガニ）に拡大した疑いがあり、死者600人・確定症例1,759人に達している上、承認済みワクチン・治療薬がなく、資金不足や治安不安により対応能力も懸念されるためフルRRAへ移行すべき。
triage.notes: Bundibugyoエボラウイルスに対する承認済みワクチン・治療薬が存在せず、臨床試験が開始されたばかりである点、医療従事者への未払い賃金による抗議活動やブニア空港閉鎖による対応遅延など、管理可能性に強い懸念がある。

article.articleHeadline: L'épidémie actuelle d'Ebola se propage plus rapidement que toutes les précédentes, selon l'agence de santé de l'UA
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The current Ebola outbreak is spreading faster than all previous ones, according to the African Union's health agency.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease, Bundibugyo strain, is spreading in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) after being declared on 15 May 2026. Africa CDC warns the outbreak is expanding faster than any prior one. As of 7 July 2026, DRC reports 1,759 confirmed cases and 600 deaths; neighboring Uganda has 20 confirmed cases and 2 deaths, with the situation described as stable. The eastern DRC outbreak centers on Bunia, Ituri, where patients are treated at Ebola Treatment Centers. The DRC has had 17 Ebola epidemics, but Bundibugyo has no vaccine or specific treatment. The WHO flagged the scale and rapid spread on 19 May. MSF expressed concerns in mid-June about notable gaps in the response. The epicenter is compared to the 2013–2016 West Africa outbreak, the deadliest in history, with over 11,300 deaths among about 29,000 cases, mainly in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone.

triage.headline_ja: 現在のエボラ流行、アフリカ連合保健機関によれば過去のどの流行よりも速く拡大
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ(ブンディブギョ株)流行が過去最速のペースで拡大し、致死率も高く、ワクチン・特異的治療法が存在しないため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: 記事はDRC（特にIturi州Bunia）とウガンダでの感染拡大を主題としているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。シエラレオネ・リベリア・ギニアは2013-2016年流行との比較で言及されているのみで現行イベントの発生地ではないため除外。ワクチン・治療法の不在、MSFによる対応の遅れの指摘は懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: Kongo'da etkilenmemiş eyalette yeni Ebola vakalarından şüphe
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Suspicion of new Ebola cases in an unaffected province in Congo.
article.articleSummary: Two new suspected Ebola cases were reported in Kisangani, north-central Kisangani in Tshopo Province, Congo, signaling spread to previously unaffected Kongo regions. The ongoing outbreak, caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, has 1,759 confirmed infections and 600 deaths. Of the two Kisangani cases, one is linked to Ituri’s Nia-Nia health zone; the other has no identifiable geographic link. WHO Congo representative Anne Ancia notes transmission continues due to population movement and insecurity, with treatment centers near capacity. Health workers in Ituri report pay delays since the outbreak was declared; Bunia officials say funding gaps and Bunia airport closure hinder response. The outbreak was officially declared on May 15 after weeks of undetected transmission. Researchers began a clinical trial last week in hopes of finding a cure.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴで感染していなかった州で新たなエボラ疑い例
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で進行中のエボラ流行（累計1,759例・600人死亡）が、これまで感染のなかったチョポ州キサンガニに拡大した疑いがあり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: 既存の大規模エボラ流行（Bundibugyo species）が新たな州（Tshopo/Kisangani）へ拡大した疑いがあり、資金不足・空港閉鎖・保健従事者の給与遅延など対応能力の逼迫が報告されている。フルリスク評価への移行が妥当。

article.articleHeadline: കോംഗോയെ ഭീതിയിലാഴ്ത്തി എബോള വൈറസ് ബാധ
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola virus infection terrorizes Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease is spreading rapidly in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with Kinshasa reporting 1,759 total cases and over 600 deaths. In the last 24 hours, 51 new cases and 20 deaths were recorded, signaling intensified transmission. Two symptomatic cases have emerged in Kisangani, one of Congo’s largest cities, but laboratory confirmation is pending and not yet in official tallies. One confirmed link points to Ny-Ni village in Ituri province; the second case has no clear geographic link to other outbreak areas, raising concerns about spread to new regions. With the outbreak worsening, frontline health workers—especially in Ituri—are striking over unpaid salaries, further hindering the public health response. Keywords: Ebola, Congo, Kinshasa, Kisangani, Ituri, Ny-Ni village, outbreak, health worker strikes.

triage.headline_ja: エボラウイルス感染がコンゴを恐怖に陥れる
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱の大規模流行が進行中（累計1,759症例、600人以上死亡）であり、新規感染地域への拡大懸念と医療従事者ストライキによる対応能力低下が重なり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: キサンガニでの症例は検査確認待ちであり、地理的リンク不明の症例が新規地域への拡大リスクを示唆。医療従事者のストライキが公衆衛生対応をさらに困難にしている点も重要。

article.articleHeadline: کنگو به موارد جدید ابولا در استان پیشتر درگیر‌نشده مشکوک است
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DR Congo suspects new Ebola cases in a province not previously affected.
article.articleSummary: As of 9 July 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo reports suspected new Ebola cases in Kisangani, a city in Tshopo province bordering Ituri, where the outbreak began. The ongoing outbreak caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus has reached 1,759 confirmed cases and 600 deaths nationwide. Two suspected cases were identified in Kisangani; one is linked to Ituri's Niania health zone, the other has no clear link to known hotspots. WHO notes the virus continues to spread, aided by population movement and insecurity, with several treatment centers nearing capacity. Healthcare workers in Ituri report unpaid salaries since the outbreak’s declaration, limited equipment, and tensions with intervention teams. Bunia airport closure hampers the response and transfer of resources. The Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccine or treatment; a Phase 1 trial began recently.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ、以前は被害のなかった州で新たなエボラ疑い例
triage.triage_reason: DRCで確認済み1,759症例・600人死亡という深刻なエボラ流行が、これまで影響のなかったTshopo州（Kisangani）にも拡大する疑いがあり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 発生地域にMaliが含まれているが、記事サマリーには言及がなくBluedotの地域付与誤りと判断し除外した。ワクチン・治療薬未承認のBundibugyoエボラウイルスによる流行で、医療従事者への未払い給与や空港閉鎖による対応の遅延など、対応能力に懸念がある。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola-utbruddet i Kongo er det raskest voksende noensinne
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak in the Congo is the fastest-growing ever.
article.articleSummary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is the fastest-growing on record, with at least 600 deaths and 1,759 confirmed cases. The deadly virus, including the Bundibugyo variant, has spread into areas of eastern Congo previously unaffected, expanding the geographic footprint and challenging health systems already stressed by conflict and underfunded care. The Bundibugyo strain carries a mortality of roughly 30–50% and currently has no approved vaccine or specific treatment. WHO warned the outbreak is not under control and continues to move into new areas, driven by human movement and overburdened clinics. First identified less than two months ago, protests erupted outside at least three treatment centers over unpaid wages and working conditions. Earlier, WHO reported over 70 health workers infected and 17 dead. Historical note: the Zaire variant caused about 11,000 deaths in West Africa a decade ago.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行は過去最速の拡大を見せている
triage.triage_reason: 致死率30-50%のエボラ(ブンディブギョ株)がコンゴ東部で急速拡大し、死者600人以上、医療従事者感染も多数発生。WHOが制御不能と警告しており、国際的拡大リスクと深刻な公衆衛生影響が認められるためフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: Angolaは発生地域に含まれるが記事サマリーではDRC国内の流行拡大が主題であり、Angolaでの発生は明記されていないため除外。ワクチン・治療薬未承認、医療従事者の感染死亡、抗議活動発生など複合的なリスク要因が確認される。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak is 'fastest growing ever' as 600 die
article.articleSummary: DRC's Ebola outbreak (Bundibugyo strain) is the fastest-growing Ebola event on record, with 1,759 laboratory-confirmed cases and 600 deaths since mid-May (case fatality rate 34%). It centers in Ituri province and affects four provinces; the virus likely circulated undetected for some time and has no approved vaccine or treatment for Bundibugyrou. Recovery stands at 285; 304 suspected cases are under investigation. Transmission occurs via close contact and infected bodily fluids, causing viral haemorrhagic fever. The response faces persistent insecurity and fragile health systems. About 700 beds across 22 treatment centres are in use (90% capacity), with plans to add 300 beds. Laboratory capacity has risen from 30 tests/day in Kinshasa to over 2,000/day in decentralised labs. WHO seeks $115 million; 32% has been received. A trial of MBP134 and remdesivir began July 2, as clashes in South Kivu risk displacement.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ流行は「史上最速の拡大」、死者600人に
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最速拡大とされるエボラ(ブンディブギョ株)流行が発生し、致死率34%、複数州に拡大、ワクチン・治療薬未承認、治安不安による対応困難があり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 承認されたワクチン・治療薬がないブンディブギョ株による流行で、史上最速の拡大速度と報告されている。WHOは1億1500万ドルの資金を要請しているが32%しか受領しておらず、国際支援が急務。南キブでの武力衝突による住民避難リスクも懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: 600 dead in DR Congo Ebola outbreak
article.articleSummary: DR Congo’s Ebola outbreak has 1,759 confirmed cases and 600 deaths, concentrated in Ituri province across four provinces. Uganda has 2 deaths and 17 recoveries among 20 cases. The case fatality rate in DRC is 34%. In-country, 285 recovered and 304 suspected cases remain under investigation. The outbreak is driven by Bundibugyo Ebola, for which there are no approved vaccines or treatments; a trial of MBP134 and remdesivir began July 2. Transmission remains ongoing in the expansion phase, hampered by population movements, insecurity, and a fragile health system. About 700 beds across 22 treatment centres are active, with plans to add 300 more; over 10,000 contacts are monitored (82% follow-up). Lab capacity has risen to 2,000 tests per day. WHO seeks $115 million to bolster the response (32% received). South Kivu has seen clashes with the M23 group, raising displacement concerns.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクで600人死亡
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準を複数満たす大規模エボラアウトブレイク（死者600人、致死率34%、越境拡大）であり、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ウガンダへの越境拡大が報告されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。南キブ州ではM23武装勢力との衝突による人口移動が感染拡大リスクを高めている。

article.articleHeadline: Κονγκό: ύποπτα κρούσματα Έμπολα σε νέα επαρχία

One of the suspected cases is linked to the Nyia-Nia health zone in Ituri province; the other has no obvious geographic link to known foci. The outbreak continues to spread, driven by population movement and insecurity, with treatment centers nearing capacity. Health workers in Ituri report they have not been paid since the outbreak was declared. Bunia airport closure is hindering response and funding flows. Authorities note attacks by angry residents and public distrust of the virus. The outbreak, declared May 15 and caused by Bundibugjo (Bundibugyo) ebolavirus with no licensed vaccine or treatment, saw last-week initiation of a clinical trial to explore therapies.

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo Ebola outbreak remains "very active," peak not yet in sight: health minister
article.articleSummary: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak remains in a 'very active' phase, and it is still too early to determine when infections will peak, Health Minister Roger Kamba said Thursday. He spoke during a visit to Bunia, the capital of Ituri Province and epicenter of the outbreak, with remarks circulated in a health ministry video as response operations approach two months. Kamba emphasized ongoing activity despite containment efforts, citing high population density, frequent population movement, and local factors that complicate community engagement as key challenges hindering peak forecasting. The remarks underscore uncertainty about the outbreak trajectory and difficulties in implementing public health measures in affected communities. The article does not provide specific case or death counts.

article.articleHeadline: Stochastic Models Reveal Rapid Smallpox Spread and High Indigenous
article.articleSummary: Smallpox spread among Indigenous Australians was likely introduced in southeastern Australia in the late 1780s, with a rapid, geographically concentrated outbreak beginning around 1789. Using stochastic multipatch epidemiological models across communities, researchers tested whether initial entry came via Makassan Indonesians in the north or settlers in the southeast. Under plausible transmission, a Makassan-origin northward spread would be too slow and limited; southeastern introduction matches historical records of swift, widespread mortality. The model estimates a smallpox case fatality around 60%, producing an approximate death toll of 220,000 Indigenous Australians. The findings argue against a continent-wide epidemic and emphasize heterogeneity in colonial impacts. The work integrates historical accounts with mathematical modeling, highlighting ongoing intergenerational trauma and the importance of accurate reconstruction for truth-telling and reconciliation across Indigenous communities and public health discourse.

article.articleHeadline: Saúde orienta população sobre prevenção à malária e febre amarela durante período de férias - Conexão Tocantins - Portal de Notícias
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Health advises the public on malaria and yellow fever prevention during the vacation period - Conexão Tocantins - News Portal
article.articleSummary: Palmas, Brazil, launches a campaign 'Enjoy Holidays without Malaria and Yellow Fever' to prevent malaria and yellow fever during peak vacation season. Educational blitzes will occur Fridays in the morning, and 5–6 p.m. blitzes at city exits, plus health education at the bus station, airport, hotels, and fishing/nautical venues. Led by Environmental Surveillance and Epidemiological Surveillance, the initiative emphasizes vaccination, mosquito bite protection, and early symptom recognition. Palmas has had no local malaria transmission since 2006, but imported cases occur; in early 2026, 22 suspected malaria notifications with 2 confirmed, matching 2025 totals. For yellow fever, vaccination remains the most effective prevention; epizootic surveillance in non-human primates monitors virus circulation. Prevention tips: up-to-date yellow fever vaccination, Anvisa-registered repellents, long sleeves and pants, screens, and avoiding outdoor activity late afternoon to dawn. Seek care promptly for fever, chills, headache, nausea, vomiting, sweating, fatigue, or loss of appetite after travel.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak spreading faster than previous outbreaks
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is spreading faster than previous outbreaks, according to Africa CDC. Wessam Mankoula, head of preparedness and emergency response, said the virus is outrunning the response and spreading faster than the resources mobilized to control it. The World Health Organization’s situation report as of July 7, 2026 records 1,759 confirmed cases and 600 deaths since the start of the current outbreak in the DRC. The report highlights ongoing transmission but provides no details on laboratory confirmation methods, infection source, or any imported/exported cases. The situation remains active as of July 9, 2026.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ流行、過去の流行より速いスピードで拡大
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の大規模流行(症例1,759件、死亡600件)がDRCで過去より速く拡大しており、公衆衛生上の深刻性・国際的拡大リスクともに高いためフルRRAへ進むべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: Africa CDCおよびWHO状況報告に基づく情報。致死率は約34%(600/1759)で高く、感染拡大速度が対応リソースを上回っている点が特に懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: കോംഗോയില്‍ എബോള വ്യാപനം രൂക്ഷം; മരണം 600 കടന്നു, ശമ്പളമില്ലാത്തതില്‍ പ്രതിഷേധിച്ച് ആരോഗ്യപ്രവര്‍ത്തകര്‍
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in Congo is severe; death toll has crossed 600, healthcare workers protest over unpaid salaries.
article.articleSummary: Kinshasa confirms an ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 1,759 cases and 600 deaths. In the last 24 hours, 51 new infections and 20 deaths were reported. Two cases in Kisangani showed Ebola-compatible symptoms; laboratory results are pending and will be added to the official tally when confirmed. One of those cases is linked to a village in Ituri province; the other has no clear geographic linkage outside Kisangani, raising concerns about spread to new areas. Health workers, mainly in Ituri, protested over unpaid salaries, threatening an indefinite strike if pay is not issued within 24 hours. They cited shortages of safety equipment and perceived discrimination. Trials for the Bundibugyo ebolavirus variant are underway, with no approved vaccine for this strain; rapid clinical testing is deemed critical by health experts.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ感染拡大が深刻化；死者600人超、給与未払いで医療従事者が抗議
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRCで1,759症例・600人超の死者を出し拡大継続中で、新地域への波及懸念や医療体制の脆弱化（給与未払いによるスト脅威）もありIHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: Bundibugyo型エボラウイルス変異株に対する承認済みワクチンがなく、臨床試験が進行中である点、給与未払いによる医療従事者のスト脅威が対応能力を著しく損なうリスクがある点に注意が必要。Kisanganiでの新規症例は地理的リンク不明でさらなる拡散の可能性を示唆。

article.articleHeadline: Congo, sospetti nuovi casi di Ebola in provincia finora risparmiata
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DR Congo: Suspected new Ebola cases in a province that has so far been spared.
article.articleSummary: Ebola cases emerge in DR Congo's previously spared regions as two suspected infections are reported in Kisangani, Tshopo province; one case is linked to Nia-Nia health zone in Ituri, the other has no clear link to known foci. The government says the latest outbreak has caused 600 deaths, with 1,759 confirmed cases nationwide. The spread continues, driven by population movements and insecurity, while several care centers near capacity. Health workers in Ituri protest delayed salaries since the outbreak was declared, compounding challenges of working with insufficient equipment. Bunia airport closure hinders response and delays fund transfers, according to local authorities. The Congolese government declared Ebola on May 15 after transmission went undetected for weeks, and Bundibugyo virus is responsible, for which there are no vaccines or approved therapies. Researchers began a highly anticipated clinical trial last week to identify a therapy.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国：これまで被害がなかった州でエボラ出血熱の新規疑い症例
triage.triage_reason: エボラ死者600人・確定症例1,759人に達し、これまで未感染だったチョポ州（キサンガニ）へ拡大。ワクチン・承認治療法がないブンディブギョウイルス株であり、国際的拡大リスクと深刻な公衆衛生影響が認められる。
triage.notes: ブンディブギョウイルスによるエボラ流行で、承認済みワクチン・治療法がない。人口移動や治安不安により感染拡大が継続し、医療従事者の給与遅配や空港閉鎖が対応を阻害している。臨床試験が開始されたばかりで今後の推移を要注視。

article.articleHeadline: L'épidémie d'Ebola se propage plus vite que les précédentes
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak is spreading faster than previous ones.
article.articleSummary: Outbreak of Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo declared May 15 is spreading faster than any prior outbreak, according to Africa CDC emergency head Dr. Wessam Mankoula. The current outbreak, involving Bundibugyo virus, has produced 1,759 confirmed cases and 600 deaths in the DRC to date. Neighboring Uganda reports 20 confirmed cases and 2 deaths, with the situation described as stable. The World Health Organization's situation report dated July 7 notes the rapid expansion and ongoing challenge to containment. Since the May 19 alert, concerns have grown about the scale and speed of transmission, with MSF warning mid-June of dangerous gaps in the response. Notably, there is no vaccine or specific treatment for Bundibugyo Ebola virus. By comparison, the 2013-2016 West Africa outbreak caused over 11,300 deaths among about 29,000 cases, the deadliest on record.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ流行は過去のものより速いスピードで拡大している
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ（ブンディブギョウイルス）流行が過去最速で拡大しており、1,759症例・600死亡と深刻な公衆衛生影響があり、ウガンダにも拡大していることから国際的拡大リスクも認められる。
triage.notes: ウガンダも感染確認地域だが対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には記載していない。ワクチン・特異的治療法がないブンディブギョウイルス株であり、MSFも対応の遅れを警告している点に留意。

article.articleHeadline: Epidemia de Ébola está a propagar-se mais rapidamente que qualquer outra anterior
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola epidemic is spreading faster than any previous one.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak officially declared on May 15 in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has already caused more than half a million deaths. A July 6 ministry bulletin, with data through July 4, records 1,561 confirmed cases and a case-fatality rate of 32.4%. About 628 patients remain in isolation or hospitalized, and 253 have recovered. The epicenter is Ituri Province, which borders Uganda and South Sudan, with spread to North Kivu and South Kivu provinces. The outbreak has also reached Uganda, reporting 20 infections, including 15 imported from the DRC, with two deaths. The cross-border spread underscores ongoing transmission needs and the importance of cross-border surveillance and containment in the affected regions.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱の流行、過去のどの流行よりも速く拡大
triage.triage_reason: DRCで発生したエボラ出血熱がウガンダへ越境拡大し、致死率32.4%と高く、公衆衛生上深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクが確認されるためフルRRAへ進むべき事案。
triage.notes: 記事中の「50万人以上死亡」という記述は他の疫学データ（1,561症例、致死率32.4%）と整合しない可能性があり、数値の信頼性は要確認。ウガンダ・南スーダンは対象国リスト外のため verified_locations から除外。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak is 'fastest growing ever' as 600 die
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-07-09, Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, caused by the Bundibugyo species, is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak ever; 1,759 confirmed cases and 600 confirmed deaths; case fatality rate 34%; 285 recovered; 304 suspected under investigation. The northeastern outbreak spans four provinces, focused on Ituri province. A trial began July 2 in DRC for MBP134 (monoclonal antibody) and remdesivir, alone and in combination. The virus spreads through close contact and infected bodily fluids; no approved vaccine or treatment exists for Bundibugyo. By comparison, the 2013-16 West Africa outbreak had 994 cases in the first six weeks, whereas this outbreak has 1,596 cases in the same period, indicating a lag in response. WHO figures accompany the update.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ発生、600人死亡し「史上最速の拡大」
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で史上最速拡大とされるエボラ(ブンディブギョ株)アウトブレイクが4州に拡大し、致死率34%・600人死亡と深刻。IHR基準の複数該当かつ国際的関心・支援の必要性が高い。
triage.notes: アンゴラは発生地域リストに含まれるが、記事サマリーではDRC国内(4州、Ituri中心)の流行のみが言及されており、アンゴラでの発生は記載なしのため除外。承認済みワクチン・治療薬が存在しない点も懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: Gefährliche Krankheit: Ebola-Fälle im Kongo innerhalb einer Woche um 25 Prozent gestiegen
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dangerous disease: Ebola cases in the Congo have risen by 25 percent within a week.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of Congo Ebola outbreak worsens: Ebola cases have risen 25 percent in one week, with 1,759 lab-confirmed cases and 600 deaths since the outbreak began in May, per Africa CDC adviser Wessam Mankoula and the Congolese government. Bed capacity is near collapse, with 95 percent of Ebola beds occupied; authorities say beds must be increased by about 50 percent immediately. Uganda example shows limited containment, with 20 cases linked to the outbreak and 2 deaths; currently 1 patient under treatment in Uganda. Congo now reports about 2,000 Ebola tests per day, though regional disparities persist. Delays remain: information on suspected cases arrives more than 72 hours after symptom onset in over half of cases, and sampling/transport is slow. The virus transmits by direct contact with bodily fluids; Bundibugyo-type Ebola lacks a vaccine or approved therapy, though two antiviral therapies are in clinical testing since last week.

triage.headline_ja: 危険な感染症：コンゴのエボラ症例が1週間で25%増加
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ症例が急増（1週間で25%増）し、病床がほぼ満床で管理体制が逼迫、ウガンダへの越境拡大も確認されているためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ウガンダも患者確認・死亡例ありと報告されているが、対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。ワクチン未承認のBundibugyo型エボラであり、抗ウイルス薬2種が臨床試験中との情報あり。

article.articleHeadline: A chromosome-level, gap-free genome assembly of the fish parasite Trypanosoma larimichthysi from large yellow croaker - Scientific Data
article.articleSummary: Trypanosoma larimichthysi, a marine fish trypanosome causing severe trypanosomiasis outbreaks in farmed large yellow croaker (Larimichthys crocea) along the Chinese coast, has a chromosome-level, gap-free genome assembly. Using PacBio HiFi long reads and Hi-C, the genome spans 51.04 Mb across 35 pseudochromosomes, with a contig N50 of 1.43 Mb and 97.96% anchored. Telomere-to-telomere resolution is achieved for 25 chromosomes (58 telomeric loci), and HiFi read mapping rate is 99.99% with >99% BUSCO completeness. The assembly encodes 10,172 protein-coding genes; repetitive sequences account for 50.33%, dominated by LINE and LTR retrotransposons. Phylogenetically, it lies within Trypanosoma, with lineage-specific gene family expansions potentially linked to host adaptation and pathogenicity. This reference-grade genome enables studies of parasite evolution, antigenic variation, and disease management in mariculture.

triage.headline_ja: 養殖ヒメコダイ（キグチ）の魚類寄生虫Trypanosoma larimichthysiの染色体レベル・ギャップフリーゲノムアセンブリ - Scientific Data
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は魚類の養殖トリパノソーマ症原因寄生虫のゲノム解析に関する基礎研究論文であり、ヒトや公衆衛生への影響は無く、水産養殖分野の学術情報に留まる。
triage.notes: 疾患名にTrypanosoma bruceiが紐付けられているが、実際の記事内容はヒト寄生虫ではなく養殖魚類（キグチ）の魚類トリパノソーマ（T. larimichthysi）のゲノム解析論文であり、ヒト感染症とは無関係。

article.articleHeadline: Bhopal Steps Up Dengue, Malaria Prevention Drive - visionmp.com vision mp - Vision MP - MP Breaking News, Madhya Pradesh News, Live Updates
article.articleSummary: Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh reports intensified prevention of dengue, malaria and chikungunya. From January to July 9, health teams surveyed 224,434 houses; mosquito larvae were found in 5,269 houses. They inspected 1,647,992 water containers, detecting larvae in 5,776 containers; 2,181 containers were emptied and larvicide added to 3,595. Malaria testing covered 121,039 people with 4 confirmed cases; dengue suspicion involved 2,730 suspects with 44 positives; chikungunya involved 615 suspects with 9 confirmed. The District Malaria Office conducts larva surveys across all city zones and runs awareness activities at schools, anganwadi centers, and clinics to curb breeding by removing stagnant water. From July 9, a special awareness drive will operate in 35 tribal hostels to educate students on prevention. Campaigns will continue through the monsoon season to reduce dengue, chikungunya and malaria risk.

triage.headline_ja: ボパールでデング熱・マラリア予防対策を強化
triage.triage_reason: 季節性の媒介蚊対策・予防活動に関する定例的な報告であり、症例数も少なく異常な流行拡大の兆候は見られない。
triage.notes: 地方保健当局による通常の予防・サーベイランス活動の報告記事。季節性(モンスーン期)の媒介蚊対策として継続的な曝露リスクはあるが、症例数は少なく重大な公衆衛生上の懸念には該当しない。

article.articleHeadline: Mexico's response to Iowa pseudorabies taking toll on US pork exports
article.articleSummary: Pseudorabies outbreaks in Iowa and Texas herds in April triggered Mexican restrictions that cut U.S. pork exports to Mexico by 17% in volume in May and by value to $185.7 million, a $30 million drop from a year earlier. Five Iowa sows tested positive on April 30; the USDA traced infections to an infected Texas outdoor herd with feral-pig contact, while the disease remains prevalent in feral hogs though eradicated in commercial herds since 2004. In June, Iowa officials said testing confirmed containment, with about 100 pigs destroyed at a central Iowa facility to prevent spread. Mexico recently relaxed some offal restrictions, permitting shipments from states other than Iowa and Texas, but verification and Iowa's importance keep exports limited. USMEF CEO Dan Halstrom urged full lifting of restrictions, citing ongoing losses as Mexico is a top market for pork offal after China.

triage.headline_ja: メキシコのイオワ州偽狂犬病への対応、米国豚肉輸出に打撃
triage.triage_reason: 本事案は米国（アイオワ州・テキサス州）の豚偽狂犬病（人獣共通感染症ではない家畜疾病）による対メキシコ貿易への影響に関するものであり、対象国（中国等）は輸出市場としての言及に留まり、実際の発生国でもない。公衆衛生上のリスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 偽狂犬病（Pseudorabies）はブタの疾病であり、ヒトへの感染性はほぼない。記事は米国・メキシコ間の豚肉貿易への経済的影響が主題であり、対象国リストに含まれる国での発生ではないため、verified_locationsは空とした。

article.articleHeadline: Actuala epidemie de Ebola se răspândește mai rapid decât toate cele anterioare, anunță Africa CDC
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The current Ebola outbreak is spreading faster than all previous ones, Africa CDC announces.
article.articleSummary: As of July 9, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has caused 600 deaths, according to the World Health Organization's latest tally compiled from information provided by Congolese health authorities, AFP reports. Africa CDC says this outbreak is spreading faster than all previous Ebola outbreaks. Ebola is transmitted through contact with bodily fluids and causes hemorrhagic fever. The tally reflects data compiled by WHO from national authorities; AFP cites this update. The available update confirms ongoing transmission in the DRC, with no further details in the excerpt about case counts beyond the death toll or specific containment actions.

article.articleHeadline: 民主剛果伊波拉疫情狂燒 短短3天再奪百命
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak rages in the Democratic Republic of the Congo; in just three days it has claimed hundreds of lives.
article.articleSummary: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) continues in the northeast, with four provinces affected and a concentration in Ituri Province. WHO figures show 1,759 laboratory-confirmed Ebola cases since mid-May, 600 deaths (case fatality rate 34%), and 285 recoveries; 304 suspected cases are under investigation. The death toll surged by about 100 in three days, from 500 to 600. Neighboring Uganda reports 20 confirmed Ebola cases, with 17 recoveries and 2 deaths. The report relies on WHO-provided data from the DRC health authorities as of July 9, 2026. The article notes ongoing transmission and the cross-border risk to Uganda, underscoring the need for continued public health measures and surveillance.

article.articleHeadline: Congo : le bilan d'Ebola atteint 600 morts, nouveaux cas dans une province épargnée
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Congo: Ebola death toll reaches 600, new cases in a province that has been spared.
article.articleSummary: As of July 9, 2026, Congo reports 1,759 confirmed Ebola cases and 600 deaths. New suspected cases have been detected in Kisangani, Tshopo province, central-north Congo, near Ituri where the outbreak began. One suspected case is linked to the Nia-Nia health zone in Ituri; the other has no apparent link to known foci. The virus continues to spread, fueled by population movement and insecurity, with several treatment centers nearing capacity, according to WHO representative Anne Ancia. Healthcare workers in Ituri report salary delays since the outbreak declaration, working with limited equipment and facing perceived unfair treatment by authorities and response teams; Bunia airport closure hampers response and fund flows. Attacks by residents and skepticism about the virus add to challenges. The outbreak, declared May 15, is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which no vaccine or treatment is approved; a clinical trial was launched last week.

article.articleHeadline: Surto de ebola se propaga 'mais rápido' do que os anteriores
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak spreads 'faster' than previous outbreaks.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is spreading faster than previous outbreaks, per Africa CDC. The current outbreak has 1,759 confirmed cases and 600 deaths, per WHO situation report dated July 7. In neighboring Uganda, the situation is stable, with two deaths for every 20 confirmed cases. The 2013–2016 West Africa outbreak remains the deadliest in history, with over 11,300 deaths among about 29,000 cases, predominantly in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ発生、過去の流行より『速い』拡大を見せる
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクが過去の流行より速いペースで拡大しており、多数の死者・感染者が確認され、隣国ウガンダにも拡大している。IHR基準を複数満たすためフルRRAへ進むべき。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak is 'fastest growing ever' as 600 die
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is the fastest-growing ever, with 1,759 confirmed cases and 600 deaths (case fatality rate 34%). The Bundibugyo species, which has no approved vaccine or treatment, is responsible; 304 suspected cases are under investigation. Declared mid-May (May 15) and focused in Ituri province across four provinces including South Kivu amid armed clashes. So far, 285 patients recovered. Laboratory capacity has risen from 30 tests per day in Kinshasa to over 2,000 daily in decentralized labs. Treatment centers total about 700 beds in 22 facilities; authorities plan to add 300 more, with centers operating at roughly 90% capacity. More than 10,000 contacts are being monitored (82% follow-up; 95% needed). The WHO seeks $115 million for the response, of which 32% has been received. Trials for MBP134 and remdesivir began on July 2.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱、史上最速の拡大で死者600人に
triage.triage_reason: 史上最速のペースで拡大するエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクであり、死者600人・致死率34%、ワクチン未承認のブンディブギョ株、武力衝突下での対応困難、WHOによる国際支援要請など複数のIHR基準・WPRO基準に該当するため。
triage.notes: 武力衝突地域での対応であり接触者追跡率が目標(95%)に対し82%と不足、資金調達も目標額の32%にとどまるなど、対応能力に懸念がある。ワクチン未承認のブンディブギョ種であることも特筆すべき異常性。

article.articleHeadline: DR Kongo: Zahl der Ebola-Fälle steigt schnell
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DR Congo: Number of Ebola Cases Rising Quickly.
article.articleSummary: Outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DR Congo) is accelerating. Since May, laboratory-confirmed cases total 1,759 with 600 deaths. Africa CDC infectious-disease physician Wessam Mankoula notes a 25% weekly rise, signaling rapid transmission. Ebola treatment beds are severely strained, with about 95% of capacity used. Uganda reports 20 Ebola cases linked to the DR Congo outbreak, including 2 deaths, and one patient remains under treatment there. Testing activity is increasing, but delays persist: in over half of cases, authorities only receive notice of a suspected Ebola case 72 hours after symptom onset, and sampling/transport delays continue. DR Congo has achieved roughly 2,000 Ebola tests per day, though regional differences exist. For Bundibugyo ebolavirus, there is no vaccine or specific therapy yet; two antiviral therapies entered clinical testing since last week.

triage.headline_ja: DRコンゴ：エボラ症例数が急速に増加
triage.triage_reason: エボラの症例数・死亡者数が急増し、国境を越えてウガンダにも拡大しており、治療キャパシティも逼迫していることからIHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: ウガンダ（Republic of Uganda）は発生地域に含まれるが、GeoNames ID 226074は対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。ワクチン・特異的治療法が未確立であり、致死率・拡大速度から高リスクと判断。

article.articleHeadline: El brote de ébola se propaga "más rápido" que los anteriores, advierte la Unión Africana
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak is spreading faster than previous ones, warns the African Union.
article.articleSummary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is spreading faster than previous waves, according to Africa CDC. A WHO situation report dated July 7, 2026, records 1,759 confirmed cases and 600 deaths in the DRC since the start of the current epidemic. In neighboring Uganda, 20 confirmed cases and 2 deaths are reported. The current outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus; there is no vaccine or specific treatment. WHO warned on May 19 about the magnitude and rapid spread in eastern DRC. The article recalls the 2013–2016 West Africa outbreak—the deadliest on record—with over 29,000 cases and more than 11,300 deaths, mainly in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱の流行、アフリカ連合が「これまでより速いスピードで拡大」と警告
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で確認症例1,759件・死亡600人、隣国ウガンダにも拡大しており、Africa CDCが過去の流行より速い拡大を警告している。ワクチン・特効薬がないBundibugyoエボラウイルスによる流行で、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事はコンゴ民主共和国（DRC）における現行のエボラ流行が主題であり、ウガンダへの拡大も言及されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。シエラレオネ・リベリア・ギニアは2013-2016年の過去流行への言及のみで現行イベントの発生地ではないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: El brote de ébola en el Congo se extiende "más rápido que nunca" y ya deja 600 muertos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak in the Congo is spreading "faster than ever" and has already claimed 600 lives.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is the fastest-growing in history, driven by the Bundibugyo strain with no approved vaccine or treatment. Since the outbreak was declared in mid-May, the WHO reports 1,759 confirmed cases and 600 deaths in the DRC (case fatality ~34%), with 285 recoveries and 304 suspected cases under investigation. The northeast of the country is affected across four provinces, concentrated in Ituri. On July 2, a clinical trial began evaluating MBP134 monoclonal antibody and the antiviral remdesivir, alone and in combination. Transmission occurs via close contact and bodily fluids. More than 10,000 contacts are being tracked (82% followed; 95% needed). Health facilities total about 700 beds in 22 treatment centers, with plans for 300 more, currently at ~90% capacity. Lab capacity rose from 30/day in Kinshasa to >2,000/day in provincial labs. WHO seeks $115 million (32% funded). Insecurity and displacement, including clashes with M23 in South Kivu, complicate response, prompting calls for ceasefire by Volker Turk.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行は「かつてないほど速く」拡大し、既に600人の死者
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3項目該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常な拡大速度、国際拡大リスク）に加え、WPRO基準も全て該当し、WHOが資金支援を要請するなど社会的・国際的関心も高いためフルRRAへ進めるべき。
triage.notes: 承認されたワクチン・治療薬が存在しないBundibugyo株による流行で、致死率約34%、紛争地域（南キブ州でのM23との衝突）による対応の複雑化が指摘されている。WHOは1億1500万ドルの資金を要請しているが32%しか確保できていない。

article.articleHeadline: Epidemia de Ébola está a propagar-se mais rapidamente que qualquer outro surto anterior
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola epidemic is spreading faster than any other previous outbreak.
article.articleSummary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is spreading faster than any prior incident, according to Africa CDC. Officially declared May 15 in the DRC, Ituri remains the epicenter near Uganda and South Sudan, with spread to North and South Kivu provinces. A 7 July WHO situation report records 1,759 confirmed DRC cases and 600 deaths; Uganda reports 20 infections and 2 deaths, 15 of which are imports from the DRC. The outbreak involves Bundibugyo Ebola virus with no vaccine or specific treatment available. MSF warned mid-June of dangerous gaps in the response as the epidemic accelerates. The article notes the DRC has seen 17 prior Ebola outbreaks. It also references the 2013–2016 West Africa outbreak, which caused over 11,300 deaths in about 29,000 cases, mainly in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ流行、過去のどの流行よりも急速に拡大
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ流行が過去最速のペースで拡大しており、複数州・国境を越えた感染（ウガンダへの越境例）を伴い、ワクチン・特異的治療法もないため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: ウガンダへの感染拡大が報告されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めない。Africa CDC・WHO・MSFが深刻な拡大とレスポンスギャップを警告しており、致死率も高い（600/1759）。

article.articleHeadline: Muertes por brote de ébola en el Congo ascienden a 600 y siguen los contagios
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Deaths from an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo rise to 600 as infections continue.
article.articleSummary: Death toll from the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has risen to 600, with total confirmed cases reaching 1,759. New suspected cases have been reported in Kisangani, Tshopo Province—the first in zones previously unaffected. One suspected case is linked to the Nia-Nia health zone in Ituri Province, where the outbreak began; the other has no apparent geographic link to known outbreaks, authorities are investigating. The government declared a new outbreak on May 15 after transmission occurred for weeks without detection, according to the World Health Organization. The current outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which there is no vaccine or approved treatment. Last week, clinical trials for a treatment began, following a long-awaited study to combat the virus.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱流行、死者600人に増加、感染は継続
triage.triage_reason: 死者600人・感染者1759人に達し、新たな未感染地域（キサンガニ）への拡大や感染経路不明の症例が確認されるなど、深刻かつ異常な公衆衛生事象であるためフルRRAへの移行が妥当。
triage.notes: ワクチン・承認された治療法がないBundibugyo型エボラウイルスによる流行で、新規感染地域への拡大や感染経路不明例が報告されており、WHOも関与している重大事案。

article.articleHeadline: فيروس نادر بلا علاج يُقلق العالم.. ما أبرز أعراضه؟
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A rare, untreatable virus is alarming the world... What are its main symptoms?
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo virus, a rare filovirus related to Ebola, is fueling a global alarm over preparedness for deadly emerging infections. In the Democratic Republic of the Congo and neighboring Uganda, as of July 9, 2026, hundreds of infections and deaths have been reported, surpassing earlier outbreaks in Uganda (2007) and the DRC (2012). The virus causes an acute febrile illness that can progress to severe inflammation, vascular damage, bleeding, and multi-organ failure. Transmission occurs via direct contact with infected body fluids, increasing risks to household members and healthcare workers. The alert is highlighted by Professor Nancy Sullivan of Boston University in an op-ed in The New England Journal of Medicine, emphasizing broader readiness for novel, potentially untreatable pathogens.

triage.headline_ja: 治療法のない稀なウイルスが世界を不安にさせている…その主な症状は？
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国とウガンダでブンディブギョウイルス（エボラ関連フィロウイルス）による数百人規模の感染・死亡が報告され、過去の流行を上回る規模であり、国際的な専門家からも警鐘が鳴らされている。
triage.notes: ウガンダも発生国として言及されているが対象国リストに含まれないため除外。米国・ボストンは専門家のコメント発信元であり発生地域ではないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: بعد وفاة 600 شخص.. الكونغو الديمقراطية تواجه أسرع تفش لإيبولا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: After the death of 600 people, the Democratic Republic of the Congo faces the fastest Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: As of July 9, 2026, Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is the fastest-spreading outbreak on record, with 1,759 laboratory-confirmed cases and 600 deaths. The northeast Ituri province remains the epicenter, with four provinces reporting cases, and the outbreak has extended to Uganda, where 20 confirmed infections have caused 2 deaths and 17 recoveries. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, a rare strain with no approved vaccines or therapies. WHO and Africa CDC warn that the true scale is still unfolding as surveillance continues, with an estimated case fatality rate around 34% among reported DRC cases. The outbreak began in mid-May 2026, and current figures are based on health authorities’ reports.

triage.headline_ja: 600人死亡後、コンゴ民主共和国は史上最速のエボラ流行に直面
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最速拡大とされるエボラ流行が発生し、ウガンダへの国際的拡大、致死率約34%、承認済みワクチン・治療法のない稀な株(Bundibugyo ebolavirus)による深刻な公衆衛生上の脅威であり、IHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていないが、国際的拡大の重要な要素として言及。稀なBundibugyo株で承認済みワクチン・治療法がないことがリスクを高めている。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola - L'épidémie actuelle d'Ebola se propage plus rapidement que toutes les précédentes
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola - The current Ebola outbreak is spreading faster than all previous outbreaks.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak declared May 15 in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is advancing faster than any previous outbreak. Africa CDC emergency director Dr. Wessam Mankoula said the virus outpaces the response, with transmission accelerating across the country. The World Health Organization’s Situation Report of July 7 records 1,759 laboratory-confirmed cases and 600 deaths in the DRC. In neighboring Uganda, 20 confirmed cases and two deaths are reported, with the outbreak described as stable. The current surge represents the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak to date, across all Ebola virus strains, not only Bundibugyo. The report highlights ongoing transmission in the DRC and cross-border concerns, underscoring the challenge of containment amid ongoing efforts.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱 - 現在のエボラ流行は過去のどの流行よりも速く拡大している
triage.triage_reason: DRCで過去最速の拡大速度を示すエボラ流行が発生し、多数の死者とウガンダへの越境拡大が確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ進める。
triage.notes: ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。ただし越境拡大の懸念は国際的拡大リスクの根拠として記載。

article.articleHeadline: 伊波拉疫情失控奪600命！WHO警告：史上傳播最快 - 民視新聞網
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak spiraling out of control, 600 dead! WHO warns: the fastest spread in history.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has reached 1,759 confirmed cases and 600 deaths (case fatality ~34%) since its mid-May declaration, making it the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak in history. The Bundibugyo strain is involved, for which there is no approved vaccine or therapy. Transmission is accelerating, with case numbers doubling roughly every 28 days, and treatment centers operating at about 90% bed occupancy. Ituri Province is the epicenter, where armed groups and insecurity hinder containment; nearby South Kivu Province faces intensified clashes, raising concerns of mass displacement and further spread. The outbreak response requires about US$1.4 billion in funding for vaccines (none approved) and broader medical and humanitarian support; WHO and Africa CDC are urging international donors to mobilize quickly to bolster manpower and resources.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ疫情が制御不能に、600人死亡！WHOが警告：史上最速の感染拡大
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がコンゴ民主共和国で1,759症例・600人死亡と急拡大し、承認ワクチン・治療薬がなく、治安悪化で封じ込めが困難なため、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当する。
triage.notes: Bundibugyo株による流行で承認ワクチン・治療法が存在せず、武装勢力による治安悪化が対応を困難にしている。WHO・Africa CDCが国際的な資金・人的支援を要請中。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola death toll in Congo reaches 600, as new cases suspected in previously unaffected provinces
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in Congo: death toll reaches 600 with 1,759 confirmed cases nationwide. New suspected cases reported in Tshopo and Haut-Uele provinces, signaling spread beyond the Ituri epicenter. In Kisangani (Tshopo), two suspected cases were identified; one linked to the Nia-Nia health zone in Ituri, the other with no apparent geographic connection. The Congolese health ministry notes that the fresh outbreak was declared May 15 after weeks of undetected transmission. The current outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus, for which no approved vaccine or treatment exists. Last week, researchers launched clinical trials for treatment. Containment is hampered by a funding gap, attacks on health centers, and ongoing eastern Congo conflict, which continues to challenge control measures in Ituri and newly affected provinces.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱、死者600人に到達 ― これまで感染のなかった州でも新規症例疑い
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョウイルス）による死者が600人に達し、感染確認地域(イトゥリ州)を超えてチョポ州・オートウエレ州にも拡大の疑いがあり、ワクチン・治療薬未承認かつ資金不足・紛争により封じ込めが困難な状況で、IHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: 承認済みワクチン・治療薬が存在しないブンディブギョウイルス株による流行で、新規州への拡大疑いと紛争・資金不足による封じ込めの困難さから、フルリスク評価が必要と判断。

article.articleHeadline: Ébola en RDC: 600 muertos y 1.759 casos confirmados
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC: 600 dead and 1,759 confirmed cases.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached 1,759 confirmed cases and 600 deaths as of July 7, with a case fatality rate of 34.1%. About 285 patients remain in isolation or hospitalization, and 750 have recovered; contact tracing stands at 80%. The outbreak—officially declared May 15 in Ituri, a border province with Uganda and South Sudan—originated in Ituri and has spread to North Kivu and South Kivu. A new development reports two additional cases in Kisangani, Kisangani city in Tshopo province (central-northern DRC); investigations are ongoing. One Kisangani case is linked to the Nia-Nia health zone in Ituri; the source of the other case remains undisclosed. The Ministry bulletin covers confirmed cases in the eastern provinces, with ongoing monitoring and response.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱：死者600人、確定症例1,759人
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で致死率34%のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクが拡大し、新たな州（キサンガニ）にも波及しているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当しフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: 発生地域にウガンダ・スーダンが挙げられているが、記事本文では国境州であることの言及のみで実際の症例発生は確認されていないため、対象国からは除外。キサンガニ（Tshopo州）への拡大が新たな懸念点。

article.articleHeadline: Ébola avança no Congo mais depressa do que a resposta: há 600 mortos e profissionais em greve
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola advances in Congo faster than the response: 600 dead and professionals on strike.
article.articleSummary: 600 people dead in the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with 1,759 laboratory-confirmed cases as of now and ongoing transmission into new areas. New suspected cases in Kisangani, in Tshopo province, one linked to Nia-Nia health zone in Ituri—the outbreak’s epicenter—and another with no clear link, suggesting undetected transmission chains. The World Health Organization warns that population movement and insecurity are fueling spread, while treatment centers approach capacity. Reuters reports 51 new cases and 20 deaths in the latest 24 hours. Health workers in Ituri have gone on strike over salary delays, harming surveillance, safe burials, and community outreach. Bunia airport closure complicates funding flows to field teams. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, a rare strain with no approved vaccines or treatments; care remains supportive while researchers launch a clinical trial for therapies.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ、対応より速く拡大：死者600人、医療従事者はストライキ
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ（Bundibugyoエボラウイルス）流行が拡大中で死者600人、確認症例1,759例、医療従事者のストライキや治療施設の逼迫など公衆衛生上・社会的に深刻な状況であるためフルRRAに進むべきと判断した。
triage.notes: 承認されたワクチン・治療法のない希少株（Bundibugyoエボラウイルス）による流行で、治安悪化・人口移動・医療従事者ストライキ・空港閉鎖など対応体制に深刻な支障が生じている。国際的な支援ニーズが高い。

article.articleHeadline: Community participation key to preventing vector-borne diseases: Officials
article.articleSummary: On July 9, 2026, Dimapur health officials and community leaders gathered at the Chief Medical Officer’s Conference Hall to prevent vector-borne diseases, focusing on Dimapur, Chümoukedima and Niuland districts with prior dengue cases. They stressed that prevention requires active community participation, given unplanned urban development and rainwater accumulation that foster mosquito breeding. The meeting emphasized source reduction: eliminate water-holding containers, keep stored water covered, maintain cleanliness, and conduct colony-level drives to remove breeding sites. Protective measures include mosquito repellents, full-sleeved clothing, and sleeping under nets; dengue should be confirmed by ELISA at government or private facilities. NVBDCP’s Dr Imnapokim noted the 2023 dengue surge was linked to El Niño, predicting a possible rise this year under similar conditions, and urged nets use and larvivorous fish release in suitable water bodies. For immediate malaria assistance, call 7630932587. Officials urged collective action to curb dengue, malaria and Japanese Encephalitis.

triage.headline_ja: ベクター媒介性疾患予防には地域社会の参加が鍵：関係当局
triage.triage_reason: 実際の症例急増や異常事態の報告はなく、地域住民向けの予防啓発会合に関する定例的な記事であるため、シグナルとして取り上げる必要性は低い。
triage.notes: 2023年のエルニーニョ関連デング熱急増を踏まえた季節前予防啓発会合であり、現時点で異常な症例増加や新規事象は報告されていない。続報でデング熱・マラリア・日本脳炎の実際の症例数増加が確認された場合は再評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ituri : 500 000 dollars du gouvernement japonais pour intensifier la réponse à l'épidémie d'Ebola - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ituri: $500,000 from the Japanese government to intensify the Ebola outbreak response - ACP.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in Ituri, Democratic Republic of the Congo, receives $500,000 from the Government of Japan via UNICEF to intensify response. On 9 July 2026, UNICEF will use the funds to acquire and distribute hygiene kits to 100 households with confirmed cases, install handwashing stations in 700 health facilities, and bolster community prevention knowledge. The six-month program also provides logistical support to decontamination teams to carry out safe, targeted community activities. The initiative aims to strengthen infection control, reduce transmission risk, and consolidate public health gains in the affected zones. Japan's funding reinforces its commitment alongside the DRC and UNICEF to protect vulnerable communities in the Ituri outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: イトゥリ州：エボラ流行対応強化のため日本政府が50万ドルを拠出 - ACP
triage.triage_reason: DRCイトゥリ州でのエボラ流行が継続しており、国際的な資金支援が行われていることから、既知のアウトブレイクの進行状況を示すシグナルとしてフルRRA対象とする。
triage.notes: 本記事は既知のイトゥリ州エボラ流行に対する日本政府の資金拠出に関するもので、新規発生や異常事態ではないが、継続的なアウトブレイクの重要な進捗情報としてピックアップ対象とする。日本は資金提供国であり発生国ではないためverified_locationsには含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Professora morre por infecção conhecida como 'doença do pombo' em Manaus
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Female professor dies from infection known as 'pigeon disease' in Manaus.
article.articleSummary: Patrícia Almeida de Lima, a 49-year-old female professor in Manaus, died from disseminated histoplasmosis, also known as the pigeon disease, with bone marrow aplasia and septicemia. The infection was contracted by inhaling Histoplasma capsulatum spores from environments contaminated with bird droppings, especially pigeons. She taught a third-year class at Escola Municipal Esmeralda Soares Neves in Manaus' North Zone. After her death, the school suspended classes and cleanup crews targeted areas with high concentrations of birds to reduce exposure risk. Histoplasmosis is caused by Histoplasma capsulatum; the fungus is commonly found in bird and bat droppings, and infection occurs when spores are inhaled during cleaning or disturbance of contaminated sites. Symptoms include fever, cough, fatigue, chest pain, and shortness of breath; severe disease can occur in individuals with low immunity.

triage.headline_ja: マナウスで「鳩病」として知られる感染症で女性教師が死亡
triage.triage_reason: 単発の個別死亡例であり、ヒト-ヒト感染しない環境由来の真菌感染症のため、国際的拡大やアウトブレイクの懸念は低い。
triage.notes: ヒストプラズマ症は環境由来（鳥・コウモリの糞便中の真菌）であり、ヒト-ヒト感染はしない。学校が一時休校し清掃対応を行ったが、局所的な公衆衛生対応にとどまる。

article.articleHeadline: Wabah Ebola di Kongo Terus Menyebar, Terdeteksi di Provinsi yang Sebelumnya Tidak Terdampak
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola Outbreak in Congo Continues to Spread, Detected in a Province That Had Been Previously Unaffected
article.articleSummary: Two suspected Ebola virus disease cases detected in Congo's provinces of Tshopo (Kisangani) and Haut-Uele on 9 July 2026, signaling spread beyond the outbreak epicenter centered in Ituri. Tshopo shares a border with Ituri and Kisangani lies near the Nia-Nia quarantine area in Ituri, suggesting possible cross-provincial transmission or proximity-related risk. Haut-Uele's link to the outbreak remains unclear, and health authorities have not disclosed case counts for Haut-Uele. The outbreak has been ongoing since May 2026. The report notes suspected cases; it does not confirm laboratory confirmation or outbreaks in the two provinces. No details on clinical symptoms, infection source, or imported/exported case status are provided in the article. Ongoing surveillance and investigation are underway.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行が拡大を続ける、これまで影響がなかった州で検出
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がイトゥリ州から新たにトショポ州・オートウエレ州へ拡大している疑い症例が報告されており、国際的拡大リスクと公衆衛生への深刻な影響が懸念されるためフルRRAに進むべき。
triage.notes: 疑い症例のみで検査確定情報なし。オートウエレ州の流行との関連性は不明であり、続報での確定情報の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Protesters burn treatment centers, attack healthcare workers to retrieve bodies of Ebola victims
article.articleSummary: EBOLA outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), first confirmed in May, has killed at least 600 people and reached at least 1,759 confirmed cases. On June 1 in Bafwabango, Ituri province, protesters burned a treatment center and a police officer was killed amid clashes over the body of an Ebola victim; attacks on health centers and Red Cross workers followed as misinformation linked the disease to hoaxes, organ harvesting, or territorial control. Burial practices and handling of deceased Ebola victims drive fear, since bodies are highly contagious and require complete wrapping. Longstanding neglect and conflict fuel distrust of foreign and central authorities, hindering responses. The outbreak is complicated by conflict in the region, with territory controlled by M23 and ISIS-affiliated Allied Democratic Forces, who are accused of politicizing and diverting Ebola funds.

triage.headline_ja: 抗議者らが治療センターを焼き払い、エボラ犠牲者の遺体奪還のため医療従事者を襲撃
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ流行は600人以上の死者と1,759例の確定症例を伴い、武力紛争や暴動により対応が著しく阻害されている。IHR基準の複数該当が認められ、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 武装勢力（M23、ISIS系ADF）による資金の政治利用や紛争地域での対応阻害が指摘されており、治安状況が公衆衛生対応をさらに複雑化させている。渡航・貿易制限の有無については記事に記載なし。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola death toll in Congo reaches 600, as new cases suspected in previously unaffected provinces
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has reached 600 deaths, with 1,759 confirmed cases nationwide. New suspected cases have been reported in the provinces of Tshopo and Haut-Uele, signaling spread beyond the Ituri epicenter. A government report published late Wednesday said two new suspected cases were identified in Kisangani, in Tshopo province; one case is linked to the Nia-Nia health zone in Ituri, while the other case has no apparent geographical connection to known outbreaks, and authorities are investigating. The health ministry notes ongoing transmission across multiple provinces, underscoring the expanding reach of the outbreak beyond Ituri. Published July 9, 2026.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ死者数600人に到達、これまで感染のなかった州で新規症例が疑われる
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRC全土で1,759例・死者600人に達し、これまで感染のなかった州（Tshopo、Haut-Uele）へ拡大しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ進むべき事案。
triage.notes: 感染経路不明の症例（geographical connectionなし）が確認されており、地域拡大や隠れた伝播鎖の可能性が懸念される。続報でWHO対応状況・国際支援要請の有無を確認する必要あり。

article.articleHeadline: 剛果爆發伊波拉疫情　醫護控訴欠薪包圍治療中心抗議 - 民視新聞網
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in Congo as healthcare workers protest unpaid wages and surround the treatment center.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s Ituri Province, centered in Bunia, with frontline health workers protesting unpaid wages as they battle the outbreak. Dozens of front-line responders gathered outside three treatment centers on Thursday, accusing the government of delaying salary payments since mid-May; police dispersed one protest outside a center. The government acknowledged administrative gaps in updating and confirming payroll lists. Africa CDC has provided about $2 million to speed payments and is working with authorities to maintain frontline morale. As of nearly two months since outbreak declaration, the DR Congo has reported 1,759 infections and 600 deaths. The World Health Organization notes a high case fatality rate of 30-50% for this Ebola strain, with no vaccine or specific antiviral available and transmission ongoing. The article does not specify the impact of protests on operations.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ流行、医療従事者が未払い賃金を訴え治療センターを包囲・抗議
triage.triage_reason: DRCイツリ州でのエボラ流行は感染者1,759人・死者600人、致死率30-50%と深刻であり、ワクチン・特効薬もなく感染が継続している。加えて医療従事者の賃金未払いによる抗議activityが対応体制に影響を及ぼす可能性があり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 致死率30-50%、ワクチン・特効薬なしという記述から、通常のザイール株とは異なる株（スーダン株等）の可能性あり。医療従事者の賃金未払い問題が対応能力に影響するリスクがあるため、続報を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: KDR: Ebola si vyžiadala už 600 obetí, podľa Africa CDC sa epidémia šíri rýchlo - Svet SME
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: KDR: Ebola has already claimed 600 lives, according to Africa CDC, the epidemic is spreading rapidly - World SME
article.articleSummary: As of July 9, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Ituri Province, northeast) is described by Africa CDC as the fastest-spreading epidemic in history. The Bundibugyo strain is responsible; there is no vaccine or specific therapy for Bundibugyo, and current vaccines targeting the Zaïre strain are only partially applicable. World Health Organization data cited 1,759 confirmed Ebola cases and 600 deaths in DRC, with the 500-death threshold surpassed just three days earlier. Clinical trials for two Bundibugyo-targeted treatments began last week. The outbreak is being compared to the 2013-16 West Africa epidemic, which recorded 994 cases in the first six weeks. In Ituri, health workers protested at three treatment centers over unpaid wages, with police dispersing one protest; authorities say payroll and response personnel issues are being addressed, with ongoing talks to avert a strike.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国：エボラで既に600人死亡、アフリカCDCによれば流行は急速に拡大中
triage.triage_reason: DRCでBundibugyo株によるエボラ流行が急速拡大し、確定症例1,759例・死亡600例に達しており、ワクチン・治療薬が不十分なため国際的拡大リスクと公衆衛生への深刻な影響が認められる。
triage.notes: Bundibugyo株は既存のザイール株対応ワクチンが部分的にしか有効でないため、対応が困難。医療従事者の賃金未払いによる抗議活動も対応能力に影響する可能性あり。Angolaは地域情報に含まれるが、記事本文では言及されていないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: El brote de ébola se propaga "más rápido" que los anteriores, advierte la Unión Africana
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak is spreading faster than previous outbreaks, the African Union warns.
article.articleSummary: Outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is spreading faster than response capabilities, Africa CDC warns. As of July 7, 2026, the DRC has 1,759 confirmed Ebola virus disease cases and 600 deaths; neighboring Uganda reports 20 cases and 2 deaths. The current outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, with no licensed vaccine or specific treatment available. The DRC has experienced 17 Ebola epidemics historically. The WHO warned on May 19 about the magnitude and rapid spread in eastern DRC. Contextual history notes the deadliest Ebola outbreak on record occurred in West Africa (2013–2016), with over 11,300 deaths among about 29,000 cases, concentrated mainly in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱の流行、過去の流行より「速いスピード」で拡大とアフリカ連合が警告
triage.triage_reason: DRCで確認症例1,759例・死亡600例、ウガンダにも拡大しており、Africa CDCとWHOが対応能力を超える速さでの拡大を警告。IHR基準複数該当かつ国際的関心が高い。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCでの流行拡大が主題。ウガンダへの越境拡大も言及されているが対象国リストに含まれないため除外。ギニア・リベリア・シエラレオネは2013-2016年の過去の流行についての文脈情報であり、現行イベントの発生地域ではないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: المركز الإفريقي يحذر: تفشي إيبولا في الكونغو الديمقراطية هو الأسرع انتشارًا على الإطلاق.. وارتفاع الوفيات إلى 600 حالة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Africa CDC warns: the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is the fastest-spreading outbreak on record, and the death toll has risen to 600.
article.articleSummary: On 2026-07-09, Africa CDC warns the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is the fastest-spreading on record, with 1,759 confirmed cases and 600 deaths since the mid-May onset. The case fatality rate is about 34% among confirmed cases. Four provinces in northeastern DRC are affected, with Ituri Province as the epicenter. The current surge surpasses all previous Ebola waves across all strains, including Bundibugyo. The World Health Organization notes the true scale remains unclear as surveillance continues and new cases appear in multiple areas. The outbreak has crossed into neighboring Uganda, reporting 20 confirmed infections, 17 recoveries, and 2 deaths. Ongoing epidemiologic investigations and contact tracing are in progress.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカCDCが警告：コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ流行は史上最速の拡大速度、死者数600人に上昇
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約34%、感染史上最速拡大、複数州に拡大し国境を越えてウガンダにも波及しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: ウガンダへの越境感染が報告されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。WHOも実際の規模は不明瞭と指摘しており、続報の注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola death toll in the DR Congo rises to 600 with over 1,700 confirmed cases
article.articleSummary: Death toll in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s current Ebola outbreak has reached 600 with over 1,700 confirmed cases as of 9 July 2026. Africa CDC calls it the fastest‑growing outbreak ever. The virus is Bundibugyo, a haemorrhagic strain with about a 34% case fatality rate per WHO data; no approved vaccine or treatments. The outbreak centers on 37 health zones in Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu, with suspected cases in Kisangani (Tshopo) and Haut-Uele indicating spread beyond the epicentre. Two potential treatments began trials on 2 July. Containment is hampered by a funding gap, attacks on health centres and staff, and ongoing eastern conflict. The WHO declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in May, after undetected spread for weeks.

triage.headline_ja: DRコンゴのエボラ死者数が600人に増加、確定症例は1,700人超
triage.triage_reason: WHOがPHEICを宣言した進行中のエボラ(ブンディブギョ株)アウトブレイクで、致死率約34%、震源地を超えた拡大が疑われており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: WHOは2026年5月にPHEICを宣言済み。Africa CDCは『史上最速で拡大するアウトブレイク』と表現。資金不足、医療従事者への攻撃、東部紛争が封じ込めを阻害。ワクチン・治療薬は未承認だが2件の治験薬が7月2日開始。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola eist in Congo al 600 doden
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola has already claimed 600 lives in Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has claimed 600 lives with 1,759 confirmed cases per WHO. The epicenter is Ituri province in eastern DRC, bordering South Sudan and Uganda. In South Sudan, no cases; in Uganda, 20 confirmed cases and 2 deaths, last case in early June. Additional cases have been reported in North and South Kivu provinces, areas largely controlled by the M23 rebels. Ongoing displacement, insecurity, and fragile health systems hinder containment. AP reports some aid workers have not been paid and lack protective equipment. The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo ebolavirus variant, for which there is no vaccine or specific treatment; clinical trials for two therapies began late last week. Belgian NGOs are scaling up operations with local partners, focusing on hygiene, infection prevention, and early detection, while warning of a severe funding shortfall and urging greater investment in prevention and local health systems.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ出血熱、死者すでに600人に
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の大規模流行（死者600人、確定症例1,759人）でウガンダにも越境拡大しており、ワクチン・治療法が確立していない変異株で紛争地域での封じ込めが困難なため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事はDRC（イトゥリ州、南北キブ州）を主体としており、ウガンダへの越境例も報告されているが対象国リストにウガンダは含まれないため除外。南スーダンは症例なしのため除外。M23反乱軍支配地域での治安不安と資金不足が対応を阻害している点にも留意。

article.articleHeadline: RDC : l'épidémie d'Ebola s'étend à de nouvelles provinces, plus de 600 morts
